title: Example 13-7: Diagrammed Scansion and Meter

illustrates.quote: Diagrammed Scansion and Meter. Follow print for spacing and punctuation of scansion and meter symbols when the text shows only a diagram consisting of accent/stress and meter signs with no lines of poetry. Use 1-3 margins for each diagrammed line.

blocks.features: Four rows of scansion symbols only (no words): two identical rows of breve/acute marks between two vertical foot pipes, then two identical rows of a leading acute, pipe, and further breve/acute groups.

print.notes: Picture on PDF p.363; a symbol-only diagram (stress marks above vertical pipes marking feet), matching rule 13.9.5's description of a diagram with 'no lines of poetry'.
print.printFeatures: Boxed inline example; four rows of breve/acute marks and vertical foot pipes, no letters. Rows 1-2: breve acute | breve breve acute | breve breve acute. Rows 3-4: acute | breve breve acute | breve acute.

braille.notes: Verbatim from .txt lines 10556-10559, after stripping a 9-space fixed left margin shared by every line of this boxed example. All four lines begin at cell 1 (1-3 margins for each diagrammed line, per rule 13.9.5); lines 1-2 are identical to each other, as are lines 3-4, matching the print's two visually-paired diagram rows.
